transcript.content:
Good morning, and welcome. MoonSafe helps you see where your money goes, build an emergency fund, and then invest step by step if you choose to.

On safety: MoonSafe does not hold your money or move it for you. Your emergency fund sits in your own onchain vault, and every deposit or purchase is something you sign in your own wallet. Nothing happens to your money without your approval.

Crypto prices can still fall a lot, so it helps to start with money you can afford to see go down. What would you like to know first: how the app works, or what an emergency fund is?

No, not yet. The $120,000 in your bank is spare money: MoonSafe doesn't track it. It only becomes Safety if you decide to set some aside as Safety.

Safety is the low-risk part of your money. Term deposits and government bonds, for example, give steadier returns that don't follow stock or crypto prices, so your whole picture falls less when markets drop.

It isn't your emergency fund, though. A term deposit is locked until it matures, so emergency money belongs in the emergency fund.

transcript.user: So what is the difference between Safety and the emergency fund? Can I use Safety in an emergency?
transcript.content: Safety is the steady, low-risk part of your money. It's meant to stop your whole picture from swinging too much when stocks or crypto fall. The emergency fund is cash for surprises: a lost job, a big repair, a medical bill. Use Safety in an emergency only if it's in a form you can withdraw without penalty; a term deposit is locked until it matures.

transcript.user: Can I count the bank money as my emergency fund? It is much easier for me.
transcript.content: Yes, you can keep your emergency money in the bank; it's still yours and still usable in a crisis. What MoonSafe can't do is count it, since it only tracks the onchain emergency fund vault. Your $50,000 in Safety is already recorded, so it shouldn't also be counted as emergency money. Money you hold outside the app for emergencies is fine, as long as it's separate from that $50,000.
